newsitem.title: UK: Mark steadies above lows on European crosses.
newsitem.headline: Mark steadies above lows on European crosses.

text.p: The mark stabilised above its lows against most European currencies with traders expecting German budget woes will ensure a broad group of countries launch European economic and monetary union.

Bonn is seen struggling to cut its budget deficit to the three percent of gross domestic product required of single currency entrants after it backed down over plans to revalue the Bundesbank's assets in 1997.
Still, German finance minister Theo Waigel offered the mark some support after he reiterated his commitment to interpreting entry criteria for European economic and monetary union strictly.
"Traders remain confident that a soft EMU will go ahead and the mark remains weak both within and outside Europe," said Avinash Persaud, currency economist at JP Morgan.
"But the market may be a bit too sanguine, and investors should take out some form of insurance by buying marks against other European currencies at these cheap levels."
Mark/French franc was quoted at 3.3705/10 at 0920 GMT from 3.3714/16 late Tuesday in Europe. The mark was at 982.30/60 lire and 84.46/49 pesetas from 982.15/45 and 84.48/50 yesterday.
Waigel's room for fiscal manoeuvre is currently limited as the Free Democrats, the junior member of the ruling coalition, oppose tax increases or extending the solidarity income surcharge.

Still, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl threatened to drop the FDP in favour of a grand coalition with the opposition parties if the FDP sticks to its guns, Germany's Die Welt newspaper reported Tuesday.
Traders viewed the report as a confirmation of political will to launch EMU on time and with a strict interpretation of the EMU entry criteria.
"EMU is worth anything to Kohl so they will forge ahead and find a way to do it," said Philippa Malmgren, European currency strategist at Bankers Trust.
Pushing ahead with tax rises may eventually be counterproductive, though, analysts said.
"Even if they find other ways of saving money, the market thinks the measures they take will keep the German economy weak," said Persaud at JP Morgan.

The fragility of the German economy was highlighted after a report showed German industrial output unexpectedly fell 1.3 percent in April with West German output down 1.4 percent from the previous month.
Reaction in the mark was muted, however, as the economics ministry said the April index was likely to be revised up. --Swaha Pattanaik, London Forex Desk +44 171 542 6284
